blocks.text: SSL pinning protects your app from security threats like man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks by verifying server certificates directly within your app.
Without it, attackers could intercept sensitive data or manipulate communications. Here’s why it matters and how to implement it effectively:
Verifies server certificates against known values.
Helps comply with Apple and Google security standards.
Keeps user data safe during transmission.
Key Steps to Implement SSL Pinning:
Ensure compatibility with iOS and Android.
Embed certificate data in your app’s settings.
Regularly update certificates and include backups to avoid downtime.

Both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store enforce strict security requirements for SSL pinning. Here’s a quick overview of their expectations:
Certificates must be updated using end-to-end encryption.
Proper validation of certificates is mandatory.
Security documentation is required during the review process.
Transparency in certificate management is essential.
Fallback mechanisms must be in place.

What are the key differences in implementing and maintaining SSL pinning for Android and iOS in Capacitor apps?
SSL pinning works a bit differently on Android and iOS, thanks to their unique APIs and security setups.

, developers often rely on network libraries like OkHttp or use native settings to set up SSL pinning. However, when it’s time to update pinned certificates, it usually means releasing a new version of the app.

, SSL pinning is typically handled via URLSession or with the help of third-party libraries. Just like Android, any updates to certificates need to be managed carefully to ensure API communication doesn’t break.
